page: Amazon Web Services m9g.metal-48xl is a general-purpose bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 96 MB of L3 cache. It has no local storage and no GPUs, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 382009.03 and a PassMark CPU score of 107871.7. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 725.94 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 329.97 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database operations are also strong, with Redis SET operations reaching 522.08 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring in the top tier. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the middle 50% at 2010.28.

While the server excels in highly parallelized workloads, it exhibits notable tradeoffs in sequential tasks and specific AI workloads. LLM text generation speeds are limited, with the small 135M model achieving only 22.59 tokens per second and the 7B model reaching 9.65 tokens per second. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. This server is configured for multi-threaded applications, large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, and parallelized data processing tasks that leverage the 192 dedicated ARM64 cores.
